products.name: Paradox (Olivia)
products.note: Conversational recruiting AI; candidate screening; automated scheduling; hiring bias risk

reading.body:
Paradox builds conversational AI for recruiting, handling candidate screening and interview scheduling while flagging hiring bias risks.

The company addresses a narrow but high-volume labor-market problem: recruiters spend hours on initial candidate filtering and calendar coordination. Automating these tasks frees hiring teams for work that requires judgment. Paradox's bias detection feature suggests awareness that AI hiring tools can perpetuate discrimination if left unchecked, a known risk when systems train on historical hiring data.

Recruiting automation sits at the periphery of AI's compute requirements. Unlike model training or inference at scale, candidate conversation and scheduling do not demand the power infrastructure that makes grid capacity the bottleneck for frontier AI. This is a workload that runs on ordinary cloud services, not new data centers built to support large language models.

The data covers Paradox's product category and stated capabilities. It does not disclose the model architecture, training data, financial backing, user base, or actual bias mitigation performance. Without those details, a reader cannot assess whether the product's AI components are proprietary or licensed, or whether bias detection is enforced or optional.

profile_text.body:
Paradox is a conversational hiring software company. According to its website, its software automates recruiting tasks including screening, interview scheduling, and onboarding, with the stated goal of moving candidates from first contact to hire faster. The company describes its AI assistant, Olivia, as handling those tasks so recruiters can spend more time with people rather than software. Paradox says it pledges to use only AI that has been thoroughly vetted and in ways that comply with principles it lists as transparent, explainable, fair, accountable, secure, and safe.

The company's tracked product is Paradox (Olivia), a conversational recruiting tool used for candidate screening and automated scheduling. The same record notes a hiring bias risk associated with that use. No lawsuits or other legal matters involving the company are recorded.
